stories.body: Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany won 43.8% of the vote in Saxony-Anhalt, more than twice its result five years earlier and far ahead of Chancellor Friedrich Merz's CDU, which received 17.2%. The party will hold 39 of 83 seats, three short of a majority, leaving an uncertain path to government because most other parties refuse to cooperate with it. AfD's state leader Ulrich Siegmund called the result historic and said the party had a mandate to govern, while the CDU reaffirmed its refusal to join it. The result is being seen as a major test of the political firewall against a party classified as right-wing extremist by domestic intelligence in the state.
stories.headline: AfD wins Saxony-Anhalt election but falls short of an outright majority

stories.body: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff made their first visit to Kyiv since Russia's full-scale invasion, meeting President Volodymyr Zelenskyy a day after talks with Vladimir Putin in Moscow. A senior Ukrainian official said the envoys brought new, more effective proposals, but the sides announced no breakthrough. Zelenskyy said he wanted wider talks involving Ukraine, the United States and European partners, while Witkoff said he hoped such meetings could be arranged soon. The discussions continue to face major disagreements over territory, and Zelenskyy warned that the war could extend through the winter, increasing Ukraine's need for air defense, energy support and LNG supplies.
stories.headline: US envoys bring renewed Ukraine peace proposals to Kyiv

stories.body: The United States and Iran have escalated attacks around the Strait of Hormuz, the strategic shipping route through which both sides are seeking to exert control. US Central Command said it struck three Iranian vessels after Iranian ballistic missiles were launched toward a US aircraft carrier and a destroyer; Iran said it had also targeted tankers using what it called unauthorized routes and warned vessels against suspicious movement. Tehran is expected to announce a restricted zone outside the strait and has threatened US energy companies. The growing confrontation at sea has further reduced prospects for diplomacy and added pressure to global energy supplies.
stories.headline: Iran threatens US energy companies as tanker conflict in the Strait of Hormuz escalates

stories.body: Israeli attacks in southern Lebanon killed at least 11 people, including children and medical workers, according to Lebanese state media and the Health Ministry. Nine people were reported killed when a residential building in Kfar Remman was hit, while a separate strike on a vehicle killed two medics; Israel also ordered residents of an area in Deir al-Zahrani to evacuate before further strikes. Israel says its operations respond to Hezbollah drone attacks and efforts by the group to rebuild military capabilities. Lebanese officials say the violence threatens a US-brokered framework intended to reduce fighting, disarm Hezbollah in designated areas and enable a gradual Israeli withdrawal.
stories.headline: Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon kill at least 11 people amid evacuation orders

stories.body: Nepal marked a national day of mourning for more than 1,300 people killed by catastrophic floods after a glacier collapse triggered a huge flow of mud and rock along the border with Tibet on August 26. Flags flew at half-mast as rescue teams continued searching for more than 5,500 missing people, including hundreds of workers at hydropower projects. Four people have been rescued in recent days, but families of missing workers have protested in Kathmandu over what they describe as an inadequate rescue effort. Authorities said they were prioritizing search operations rather than organizing wider official mourning events.
stories.headline: Nepal observes a day of mourning as searches continue after catastrophic floods

stories.body: China will inject 360 billion yuan, about $53.6 billion, into eight state-owned banks and insurers as Beijing seeks to reinforce its financial system and support a slowing economy. The package includes capital for major lenders such as Industrial and Commercial Bank of China and Agricultural Bank of China, as well as several insurers, with the aim of improving their ability to lend, absorb risks and support investment. The move comes as China confronts weak domestic demand, a prolonged property downturn, an aging workforce and trade and technology tensions with the United States. Official data showed second-quarter growth slowing to 4.3%, below the government's annual target range.
stories.headline: China prepares $54 billion capital injection for state banks and insurers

stories.body: At least five people were killed after an Amazon cargo plane overran a runway at Miami International Airport, struck multiple vehicles and caught fire, authorities said. The crash forced the closure of all runways at one of the country's busiest airports and halted flights while emergency crews responded. Investigators are working to determine what caused the aircraft to leave the runway.
stories.headline: Amazon cargo plane crash at Miami airport kills at least five people

stories.body: A federal judge in California ruled that the Trump administration cannot deport noncitizens solely for speech supporting Palestinians or criticizing Israel, finding that the government's approach violated First Amendment and due-process protections. Judge Noël Wise issued the ruling in a case brought by The Stanford Daily, whose student journalists said international students feared speaking openly because of deportation threats. The judge said free speech cannot be limited to views that complement the government, and cited immigration actions against critics of Israel's war in Gaza as well as people critical of Charlie Kirk. The Justice Department did not immediately comment.
stories.headline: Federal judge rules Trump cannot deport students for criticizing Israel

stories.body: A United Nations Environment Programme report says the world will soon exceed the temperature threshold established by the 2015 Paris climate agreement, acknowledging that some of the worst effects of global warming can no longer be avoided. The report frames the overshoot as temporary rather than irreversible and sets out a path for bringing global temperatures back below the danger threshold through deeper emissions cuts and climate action.
stories.headline: UN says global warming will temporarily exceed a key temperature limit

stories.body: US consumers have spent an estimated additional $100 billion on gasoline and diesel in the six months since the US-Israel war on Iran began, according to a Brown University tracker cited by Al Jazeera. That amounts to roughly $763 per US household, with gasoline rising 39% to about $4.15 a gallon and diesel increasing more than 60% to $5.90. The highest average gasoline prices are on the West Coast, led by California at $5.85 a gallon. Rising fuel prices also increase costs throughout food production and transport, adding pressure to household budgets.
stories.headline: High gas prices are squeezing US drivers as the Iran conflict raises fuel costs

stories.body: Spain's Council of Ministers is set to approve the declassification of intelligence reports related to the Ceuta migration crisis, with the material expected to be released Wednesday morning. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has said the documents did not predict the scale or likelihood of the mass crossings at the end of July, describing prior intelligence and Frontex warnings as routine. Defense Ministry sources cautioned that some material may remain secret to protect information shared by foreign intelligence agencies. The crisis has continued for more than a month, with thousands returned to Morocco and authorities still unable to give a precise count of those remaining in Ceuta.
stories.headline: Spain will declassify intelligence reports on the Ceuta migration crisis

stories.body: Ceuta President Juan Jesús Vivas and opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo accused Morocco of being behind the mass arrival of migrants in late July, which they described as an effort to destabilize the Spanish enclave. Vivas said police reports and images showed Moroccan gendarmerie directing people during the crossings, while Feijóo criticized the central government for its handling of the crisis and demanded a date for restoring normality. A survey for El País and Cadena SER found that nearly 90% of respondents assign Morocco substantial responsibility, while about 72% also assign substantial responsibility to Pedro Sánchez's government. The government has said it lacks solid evidence against Morocco.
stories.headline: Opposition leaders blame Morocco for Ceuta crisis as Spain debates its response

stories.body: Spain's government has launched the Casa 47 portal, a new platform for applying for public affordable-rental housing that begins with 800 homes and is expected to add another 1,500 soon. The site will show available properties, eligibility requirements, deadlines and application conditions, and includes a tool for applicants to identify homes they may be able to request. Valid applications will enter notarized lotteries, and applicants can rank multiple homes by preference. The government says rents should not exceed 30% of a household's disposable income, while initial 14-year contracts may be renewed in seven-year periods for up to 75 years if eligibility conditions continue to be met.
stories.headline: Spain launches Casa 47 public housing portal with 800 rental homes

stories.body: Barcelona's L9 and L10 Nord metro lines resumed normal service between La Sagrera and Bon Pastor after more than two months of works at the La Sagrera macropit. The two-phase project connects the northern branches to the future central section and is intended to improve the line's safety, comfort and accessibility; it has a budget of €22.6 million. An alternative bus service covered the disruption, averaging 3,295 daily validations on weekdays in July and 2,386 in August. The pedestrian interchange corridor between lines L1 and L3 at Catalunya station has also reopened after renovation and asbestos-removal work.
stories.headline: L9 and L10 Nord metro services resume between La Sagrera and Bon Pastor

stories.body: TMB has put Barcelona's first fully electric, zero-emission neighborhood minibus into service on route 185 between Canyelles metro station and Vall d'Hebron Hospital. The nearly seven-meter Yutong vehicle carries up to 26 passengers, including 10 seated, and is designed with a lower floor, ramps, accessible doors and camera-based mirrors. It is the first of five electric minibuses TMB plans to deploy in coming weeks as part of a wider €19 million order for 23 electric buses. TMB aims to continue expanding its zero-emission fleet as part of its decarbonization strategy.
stories.headline: Barcelona introduces its first fully electric neighborhood minibus

stories.body: Barcelona has begun a nearly €2 million restoration of the seven historic façades of the former Renfe workshops in Parc del Clot, structures dating from 1858 that were incorporated into the park in 1986. Work is expected to run through the first quarter of 2027 and will repair structural damage, replace lost sections, treat cracks, remove vegetation and embedded rust, and clean the façades with pressurized water. The city will also apply treatments to protect the industrial-heritage structures from moisture and graffiti. The project forms part of Barcelona's broader Pla Endreça public-space maintenance program.
stories.headline: Barcelona begins restoring historic façades of former Renfe workshops in El Clot

stories.body: Barcelona has entered the final full political year of the 2023-2027 municipal term, with parties balancing routine city business against preparations for the May 2027 election. Major unresolved issues include the 2027 budget, tax ordinances and whether to raise the tourist tax for cruise passengers staying fewer than 12 hours, potentially from €11 to €30 per person per day. Mayor Jaume Collboni may need to extend the current budget because he lacks a council majority and cannot again use a confidence motion to approve accounts. The city is also expected to address authorizing Taser use by the Guàrdia Urbana and advance the pending Diagonal tram connection between Verdaguer and Francesc Macià.
stories.headline: Barcelona begins its final political year before the 2027 municipal election
